title: Saltimbocca alla Romana
subtitle: Roman veal escalopes with prosciutto and sage
excerpt: Rome's most famous veal dish: thin escalopes pinned with prosciutto and a sage leaf, pan-fried in butter until golden, finished with white wine. The whole thing takes ten minutes and is utterly delicious.

recipe.sourceNotes: Saltimbocca alla Romana (literally 'jump in the mouth, Roman style') is one of the canonical dishes of Roman cuisine, associated with the trattorie of central Rome. The dish consists of thin veal escalopes laid with prosciutto and a sage leaf, secured with a toothpick, then sautéed in butter with the prosciutto side down first. The pan is deglazed with dry white wine, which lifts the fond and creates a brief, light sauce. The dish is intentionally simple; its quality depends entirely on the quality of the ingredients, particularly the prosciutto. In Rome, the dish is made with veal; in other regions of Italy, pork, chicken, or turkey breast escalopes are substituted. The sage must be fresh; dried sage does not work for this dish.

content.text: Do not season the veal with salt before cooking; the prosciutto provides more than enough. The escalopes go into the pan prosciutto-side down first; this crisps the ham and prevents it peeling away. The cooking time is very short: 2 minutes per side for a thin escalope. Deglaze quickly with wine and serve immediately.

items.preparation: cut into 4 escalopes and pounded thin; substitute veal escalopes if available

content.text: Lay a slice of prosciutto on each escalope. Place 2 sage leaves on top of the prosciutto and secure with a toothpick through all layers. Season the meat side only with pepper; do not salt.

Heat the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add the escalopes prosciutto-side down. Cook for 2 minutes until the prosciutto is golden and crisped. Turn and cook the meat side for 2 minutes. Remove to a warm plate.
Pour the wine into the pan and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes, scraping the fond. Spoon the sauce over the escalopes. Serve immediately with roasted potatoes or wilted greens.
